sentences.text: Researchers developed a single-pot electrochemical device that detects Alzheimer's disease biomarkers in untreated blood or plasma within 20 minutes using high-affinity antibodies and a molecular pendulum mechanism.
When an electrical potential is applied, a negatively charged DNA scaffold moves toward the electrode, allowing real-time detection and quantification of the biomarkers.
The platform was tested on 80 clinical plasma samples using the biomarkers Aβ42 and p-tau217.
Analyzing both biomarkers together performed better than analyzing just one, achieving an area under the curve of 0.9475, 82.5% sensitivity, and 92.5% specificity.
The authors state the strategy shows great potential for early Alzheimer's diagnosis in community or home settings.
